speaker: Jyotiraditya Scindia
role: Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Power
quote_english: Once that is done, India's grid, which today has 28,000 megawatts of electricity supply capability along with the Southern grid, will become one of the largest synchronously connected grids of the world.
summary: The Southern grid was synchronously connected to the national grid on 31 December 2013, creating a pan-India synchronous grid of about 232 GW that was described as one of the world's largest.

evidence.title: Indian power system becomes largest operating synchronous grid in the world
evidence.key_figure: Raichur-Solapur 765 kV line commissioned on 31 December 2013; pan-India synchronous grid of about 232 GW

analysis:
Scindia said the Southern grid's synchronous connection would make India's grid one of the largest synchronously connected grids in the world. The Raichur-Solapur 765 kV line was commissioned on 31 December 2013.

AIPEF and the Times of India reported a pan-India synchronous grid of about 232 GW. PIB described 'One Nation - One Grid - One Frequency' as accomplished and put the grid at 249 GW, one of the world's largest synchronous operating grids.

The direct quote used 'one of the largest', which the record supports. The newspaper headline's stronger 'largest' formulation is not the wording of the quoted claim.
notes: PIB and AIPEF/TOI differ on installed capacity (249 GW vs about 232 GW), likely because of different counting dates. The claim's 'one of the largest' wording is supported by both. [ingest: 1 evidence link(s) blocked/unreachable to the checker; verify manually]
